messages:
alexa: Ran an nsys capture on the repro workload, seeing recurring idle gaps right after the prefetch kernels. Perfetto export here: https://perfetto.link/trace-repro-2393 :eyes:

mike: looked at the trace — the gaps line up with a tight NVTX range boundary labeled `kv_commit`. Could be we pop the range before async work completes.

sam: the runtime starts the prefetch async and immediately NVTX_PUSH/POP around the submit call. snippet: ```cpp
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("kv-prefetch:submit");
issue_async_prefetch();
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```
That means the actual DMA/kernel work is outside the range.

alexa: exactly. we want NVTX to represent interesting GPU activity, not just API calls. Right now timeline misleads kernel selector/tail analysis. :thinking:

rachel: what's the GPU/driver? need full nsys metadata.

alexa: A100, CUDA 12.2, driver 525.60, nsys 2024.3. trace attached above.

devon: hypothesis: batching heuristic is shrinking batches when KV hits are low, which increases kernel count and amplifies the popped-range noise. Also the kernel auto-selector sometimes gates a tiny kernel variant that leaves longer CPU-side waits.

mike: agree. we should add a per-request NVTX span that wraps end-to-end request, plus inner spans that map 1:1 to kernels with unique names — that way we can correlate kernel timelines back to requests even when ranges are split.

sam: naming constraints: NVTX name limit ~128 chars, but nsys/perfetto will collapse ranges with identical names across threads. So we must embed unique request IDs. Propose shorthand naming: `r{rid}|s{seq}|k{short}`. Example: `r123|s2|kpref`. Keeps lengths small.

alexa: also add a synthetic span for "wait-for-kv" that we push when we spin/poll on CPU waiting for a KV fill. It makes the CPU-side tail visible in the trace.

rachel: small note — nsys groups ranges by name for summary charts. If we emit unique names per request we'll explode cardinality. We should emit a map artifact that translates long unique names to short canonical names for aggregated reports. I can add a tracer option to set `emit_unique_names=false` for perf runs.

devon: one more datapoint: enabling prefetch coalescing in batcher caused 95th latency to jump in the canary. I collected stack dumps. It looks like more frequent kernel launches + extra cache fills interact poorly with the kernel selector fallback path.

mike: did you try forcing a single kernel variant (no selector) to isolate?

devon: yes — forcing linear kernel reduced 95th by ~18% but avg token time went up by ~6%. So selector helps avg but may harm tail when KV latency is spiky.

sam: actionable for instrumentation:
- emit `req:{rid}` outer span per-request
- emit `k:{kid}` inner spans immediately before kernel launch and pop after cudaEventSync/completion callback
- emit `wait-kv` span on CPU between submit and cache-ready
- include `|m=<mod>|b=<batch>` suffix to capture model variant and batch size (short keys)
This should give us kernel-level and request-level correlation while keeping names short.

mike: sample encoded name: `r123|s1|kpref|m=gpt2|b=16` (~28 chars) — OK.

rachel: I'll implement a tracer toggle to collapse names for aggregated telemetry and to emit a sidecar mapping file (name->short). Also I'll add a perf artifact uploader that redacts request ids for public traces.

alexa: plan: rachel PR for tracer mapping and toggles, sam PR to runtime to push/pop spans around kernel completion callbacks and wait-for-kv, mike will run nsys sweep across kernel variants and quant profiles, devon to run canary compare and attach latency histograms.

alexa: tagging for follow-up @rachel @sam @mike @devon :point_up:

mike: FYI quick perfetto view: https://perfetto.link/trace-repro-2393

infra-bot: deploybot: canary build 2026-03-17T12:05 started (build/ci-2393) :rocket:

alexa: thanks all — let's reconvene after the tracer PR lands and we have a canonical nsys sweep.

End of thread.
